invariants: This is admission authorization for one exact operation, not evidence that its database transaction committed.
The signer must have explicit trust for this purpose, participant, privacy domain, environment, workload principal and audience; existing Identity assertion trust is insufficient.

Maker and checker are distinct current human principals; authority and step-up proof digests bind complete canonical evidence including sessions, authenticator credential identities/epochs and committed verification records.
Native replacement provenance binds the exact committed predecessor-to-successor credential transition; successor credential epoch is predecessor epoch plus one.
All source, generation, candidate, proof, predecessor trust and exact selector coverage is authenticated by its owner before signing; digest equality alone does not establish authority.

Successor trusts retain SHA256(canonical candidate) as admissionDigest. The signed statement includes the derived trust-set digest and selector-transition digest, avoiding circular witness/trust hashes.

The fenced admittedAtNs is strictly before authorizationExpiresAtNs, at most60 seconds later and bounded by all current authority, approval, provider and root-trust deadlines. Both times come from the transaction owner, not from a client.

Signature verification is historical authenticity only. Current authority, provider state, full atomic activation, approval consumption, committed readback and recovery remain durable-owner obligations.
The first successor signature may prove key use but cannot authorize its own signing grant.
External signing I/O is unsupported until its durable attempts, reconciliation and re-fencing are independently qualified.
